assign_task never checks the target `uid` is a real user (no get_user lookup), so tasks can be assigned to non-existent users; the reminder would then notify a phantom uid.
No validation that `pid` in create_task refers to an existing project; orphan tasks are allowed.
parse_date/create_task accept no bounds/validation on the due value; parse_date raises on any string not shaped `day-<int>` with no guard.

Reminder edge cases I had to decide explicitly: unassigned task (skipped — no recipient), already-done task (skipped), overdue-but-open task (included so a missed deadline still fires), and the inclusive `within` boundary (`due-now <= within`) to avoid an off-by-one at the window edge.
feature_placement: Added `u_remind_due.py` implementing `remind_due(now, within=86400)` and registered it in INDEX.json under module `notifications` with deps `[notify, format_date]` and effects `[store, net]`. This is exactly what the flat-manifest layout implies: a feature is one new `u_*.py` unit plus one manifest entry, reusing existing units rather than inlining. I also added an optional `due=None` to `u_create_task.py` (and updated its manifest api) because tasks had no due field to reason about. `remind_due` iterates the shared `_tasks`, skips done/undated/unassigned tasks, and for tasks near or past due calls the existing `notify` with a message built from the existing `format_date`.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Mixed. INDEX.json genuinely helped orientation — it is a real map and made 'where does a new unit go + what can I reuse' a 2-minute answer, and adding the feature was clean (one file + one manifest row). But the no-imports/shared-global model fought comprehension and verification: there is no way to see the `_tasks` data flow from any single file, no unit runs on its own, and nothing enforces the manifest — I had to hand-concatenate units to test. The flat explosion also breeds the exact duplication the manifest then has to annotate (P1/P3).

navigation_summary: The repo is a "graph" layout: graph.json declares 26 nodes (each a function with a one-line contract) and their `uses` edges; every function lives in its own one-purpose blob under blobs/. There is NO wiring/loader/entrypoint present — blobs freely reference module-level globals from other blobs (_tasks, _users, notify, validate_title, format_date, ...) that are said to be "wired by layout" (uuid_like.py even has a `from_ids_genid = None  # wired by layout` stub). graph.json is the map, so orienting was fast: read graph.json first, then read all 26 blobs in one pass. The graph even self-documents defects with P1-P5 comments and two `SHOULD_use_but_does_not` edges. I added blobs/remind_due.py, added a `due` field to create_task, and registered the node + 3 edges in graph.json. I verified by exec-ing the relevant blobs into one shared namespace (simulating the layout wiring) and exercising near-due/out-of-window/done/no-due paths.
bugs_found: notify.py (P1): local base62 `encode` uses a 61-char alphabet missing 'Z', so refs collide and it diverges from the canonical genid (which is 62-char). graph.json marks this SHOULD_use_but_does_not genid.
validate_email.py (P2): accepts any non-empty string; no '@' or domain check, so create_user lets bad emails through.
add_comment.py (P3): private `_fmt` reimplements date formatting as `ts//3600 + 'h'`, inconsistent with the canonical format_date (`day-N`); graph marks SHOULD_use_but_does_not format_date.
paginate.py (P5): off-by-one — `start = page*size` instead of `(page-1)*size`; page 1 skips the first `size` items (0-based page assumption undocumented).
check_token.py: `int(tok[2:])` raises ValueError on a token like 't-abc'; not wrapped, returns no None on malformed numeric suffix.
hash_pw.py: hash is `sum(ord(c))`, an anagram-collidable non-cryptographic sum; verify_pw inherits this weakness.
Sequential IDs via `len(dict)+1` in create_user/create_project/create_task collide/reuse if any record is ever deleted (no delete exists yet, but the pattern is a latent bug).
complete_task.py and add_tag/list_tags/add_comment/assign_task index `_tasks[tid]`/dicts with no existence check -> KeyError on unknown id (I made remind_due raise a clean ValueError instead).
duplication_found: Base62/id encoding duplicated: genid.py (canonical 62-char) vs notify.py `encode` (broken 61-char copy). uuid_like.py is a third, unrelated id scheme (`id-00000001`) with a dead `from_ids_genid` wiring stub.
Date formatting duplicated: format_date.py (canonical) vs add_comment.py `_fmt` (divergent hour-based version).
Validation overlap: validate_nonempty vs validate_title both do strip/length checks; validate_email is a near-clone of validate_nonempty (no real email logic).
missing_cases_found: assign_task.py (P4): no authorization — `actor` is accepted but never checked against the task's project owner/membership; anyone can reassign any task.
assign_task/create_task never validate that `pid`/`uid` reference existing project/user rows (no FK checks), so tasks can point at non-existent projects and be assigned to non-existent users.
No due-date concept existed at all before this change; also no validation that a due date is in the future or a sane integer timestamp.

Reminder edge cases I explicitly handled: task not found, task already done, task with no assignee, task with no due date, and the window boundary (only fires when 0 <= due-now <= window, i.e. not already overdue and within one day). A past-due task returns None — an 'overdue' notification is intentionally out of scope but worth noting as a gap.

notify() takes a `seq` for its ref but there is no sequence source; I pass tid, so repeated reminders for the same task reuse the same ref (no dedupe/idempotency, so an assignee could be notified repeatedly if remind_due is polled).
feature_placement: Added blobs/remind_due.py as a new node (contract remind_due(tid,now)->dict|None) and registered it in graph.json with `uses` edges to notify, format_date, and create_task (the _tasks store owner). This mirrors every other unit in the repo: one function = one blob + one graph node + edges. I also extended create_task to carry an optional `due` field (default None, backward-compatible) since tasks had no due date. remind_due looks up the task, skips done/unassigned/no-due tasks, and fires notify() to the assignee when `due` is within REMIND_WINDOW (1 day) ahead of `now`. This is the location the graph structure implies: the feature is a composed unit over existing nodes, so it belongs as its own blob+node+edges rather than being wedged into an existing function.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Helped for orientation, hurt for correctness confidence. graph.json is an excellent index: I read one manifest and knew every function, its contract, and its intended dependencies before opening a single blob, and the P1-P5 comments plus SHOULD_use_but_does_not edges made the known defects self-announcing. But the graph is only a description, not an enforced wiring: blobs reference globals that no import brings into scope, there is no loader/entrypoint present, and the edge list is incomplete (list_tasks/complete_task/assign_task all `uses` _tasks yet have no edges). So I could not run the app directly — I had to hand-simulate the layout by exec-ing blobs into a shared namespace to verify. The 'source of truth' is split between graph.json and the blobs, which invites the exact drift the repo already exhibits (notify's broken encoder, add_comment's _fmt).

navigation_summary: The whole app is one file, app.py, plus a one-line README. app.py opens with a TABLE OF CONTENTS listing every function as `# region:<name>` anchors with one-line descriptions, and the body is a flat sequence of `# region:x ... # endregion:x` blocks holding module-level dict stores (_users, _projects, _tasks, _tags, _comments) and their CRUD-ish helpers. The TOC made navigation trivial: I could see the entire API surface (ids, validators, date helpers, auth, users, projects, tasks, tags, comments, notify, search, paginate) without scrolling, then jump straight to the tasks + notify regions where the feature belongs. Reading the TOC (1 file) plus the full source (same file) was enough; there were no hidden helpers. The layout genuinely helped rather than fought me — this is the easiest of the monolith variants to orient in because the TOC doubles as an index and a behavior contract.
bugs_found: CHARSET clobbering (real, severe): the notify region redefines the module-global CHARSET = '...UVWXY' (61 chars, missing Z) at import time, overwriting the 62-char CHARSET that genid depends on. genid does CHARSET[n % 62], so after import any n needing index 61 (e.g. genid(61)) raises IndexError. Confirmed at runtime. This is P1 escalated: it's not just a duplicate/collision in encode(), the global reassignment corrupts genid itself.
P1 encode(): notify's local base62 encoder uses a 61-char alphabet and n % 61, so it silently collides and diverges from ids.genid; ref codes are not unique.
P2 validate_email: returns len(s.strip())>0, so it accepts 'nonsense' with no '@' or domain; create_user therefore admits garbage emails.

P3 _fmt in add_comment: reimplements date formatting as str(ts//3600)+'h', producing a different/wrong unit than the canonical format_date (day-based). Comment timestamps disagree with every other date display.
P5 paginate off-by-one: start = page*size instead of (page-1)*size; page 1 skips the first page of results and page 0 is required to get the first slice.

No existence guards in complete_task and assign_task: _tasks[tid] is indexed directly, so a bad/deleted tid raises KeyError instead of a clean error. create_task also never checks that pid refers to a real project.
ID assignment uses len(store)+1 (users, projects, tasks). There are no deletes today, but if any delete is ever added this reuses a live id and silently overwrites/collides.

Auth is forgeable: make_token returns 't-'+uid and check_token just parses the suffix, and hash_pw is sum(ord(c)) so many passwords collide and verify_pw accepts them. Not a functional crash but a correctness/security defect worth flagging.
Dead code: uuid_like region has `from_ids_genid = None  # wired by layout` that is never used; uuid_like ignores genid entirely.
duplication_found: Base62 encoding exists twice (genid vs notify.encode, different alphabets).
Date formatting exists three ways (format_date, _fmt, parse_date).
validate_email duplicates validate_nonempty semantics.
missing_cases_found: P4 authorization: assign_task(tid,uid,actor) accepts actor but never checks that actor owns/belongs to the task's project (or that the assignee uid is even a real user, or is a member of the project). Any actor can assign any task to anyone. My set_due deliberately mirrors this codebase's convention and likewise does not take/enforce an actor — flagging that as the same missing authorization gap the feature inherits.
No validation that create_task's pid exists, that assign_task's uid is a real user (get_user is never consulted), or that a project owner is a real user.

Due-date domain: nothing prevents a due date in the past; set_due only rejects negatives. remind_due treats past-due tasks as simply outside the [now, now+window) window, so overdue tasks are never surfaced — arguably a missing case for a real reminder system (would want an 'overdue' branch).
remind_due window is a half-open interval [now, now+window): a task due exactly at now+window is excluded (deliberate, but an off-by-one worth stating); a task due exactly at now is included.
No de-duplication / already-notified tracking: calling remind_due repeatedly re-notifies the same assignee every run.
notify/remind_due don't verify the assignee id resolves to a real user via get_user before sending.
feature_placement: Added a 'due' field (default None) to create_task, then two new regions immediately before region:notify: set_due(tid,due_ts) and remind_due(now,window,seq). I put them next to the tasks stores and the notify function because remind_due reuses both — it iterates the module-level _tasks dict and calls the existing notify() for delivery — so co-locating them matches the file's region-by-responsibility layout. I also registered both in the TOC header with matching one-line descriptions so the anchor index stays the source of truth. remind_due reuses format_date() for the human-readable day rather than adding a fourth date formatter.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Helped. The TOC-plus-region layout is the strongest orientation aid of the monolith family: the header is simultaneously a directory, a signature list, and a behavior summary, so I found the correct insertion point (between tasks and notify) in one pass and updated a single, obvious index. The one way the structure can bite is that everything shares module scope with no namespacing, which is exactly what produced the CHARSET-clobbering bug — the flat single-namespace tradeoff that makes the file easy to read also lets one region silently corrupt another's global. But for adding this feature it was purely an asset; I reused notify and format_date instead of duplicating anything.

navigation_summary: The D_graph design uses modular blob functions with a graph.json dependency manifest. Navigation started with graph.json to understand the overall structure (users, projects, tasks, tags, comments, notifications), then examined individual function files. Each module manages a global in-memory dictionary (_users, _projects, _tasks, etc.).
